articles.title: MS NOW, CNN and Politico journalists blocked from White House after Trump ban
articles.description: Journalists from MS NOW, CNN and Politico were denied access to the White House, one day after Trump banned three media outlets over their coverage of him.

articles.title: Thick smoke seen near Riyadh airport after air-raid alerts in Saudi capital
articles.description: Authorities also issued warnings for Jeddah and Yanbu, a major industrial port and home to vital oil facilities Flames and a large plume of black smoke were seen rising above Riyadh airport in Saudi Arabia on Saturday after the government sent air-raid alerts to citizens by phone overnight warning of aerial attacks. Explosions were heard in the capital and firefighters battled to extinguish the flames of a burning fuel tank emblazoned with the logo of the Saudi oil company Aramco near the city’s King Khalid international airport.

articles.title: Jewish heirs of Holocaust victims sue California museum over Nazi-looted art
articles.description: Pasadena’s Norton Simon Museum holds 16th-century paintings stolen by the Nazis during the second world war Jewish heirs of Holocaust victims and their representatives have filed two lawsuits in California staking their claims to Nazi -looted paintings that still hang on the walls of prominent museums in Los Angeles and Auschwitz. This pair of lawsuits are the first to be filed after the recent passage of laws by California and the US Congress, which strengthen US-based claims to artwork that were forcibly taken from Jewish families during the second world war.

articles.title: MS Now and CNN say their reporters were denied access to White House after Trump media ban
articles.description: President said he was banning MS Now, CNN and Politico journalists, saying of their coverage: ‘You get sick of it.’ News outlets MS Now and CNN said their journalists were denied access to the White House grounds on Saturday morning, a day after Donald Trump said he would ban them ,and the website Politico from the executive branch complex. MS Now said a reporter and a cameraman had been denied access and had their White House press passes confiscated by the US Secret Service at a security gate outside the West Wing. CNN reported that its reporter Betsy Klein was also denied access and had her press pass seized too.

articles.title: She pays $96 a month to live in Yellowstone National Park: 'Being here has changed my life'
articles.description: Zoe De La Paz quit her corporate job in Chicago and in June moved to Yellowstone to work as a seamstress.

articles.title: Flames reported near Saudi capital airport as Pakistan presses Iran over energy supplies
articles.description: Smoke and flames were seen near Riyadh’s main airport after Saudi civil-defense alerts, while Pakistan urged Iran to protect energy supplies and shipping.

articles.title: Trump’s battle to rename the Kennedy Center has put its future at risk
articles.description: The president has threatened to block renovations and suggested the landmark could be demolished after courts ruled against his bid to rename it It was born with the world premiere of Leonard Bernstein’s Mass. “Young people will come here and they will see this cultural centre,” Rose Kennedy, the mother of slain US president John F Kennedy, said at that opening night gala . “They will carry some of these ideas back to their different communities.” More than half a century later, the potential death knell came just after 4.30pm on Tuesday with a perfunctory announcement on the public address system: “The centre is now closed to the public. Please exit the centre by way of the Hall of States.” Soon barricades had been erected and security guards were blocking access.

articles.title: Likelihood of eating fresh produce increases with income for US adults, new CDC report shows
articles.description: The report highlights deep divides between low- and middle- income, a disparity that dates back decades A new report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reaffirms that adults are more likely to eat fresh fruits and vegetables as their income increases. The data brief comes as Republican cuts to food assistance programs, colloquially called “food stamps”, have led enrollment to “ plummet ”. Changes to US dietary guidelines, led by health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr , have also made a government-recommended diet more expensive. A new “food pyramid” released in January emphasized animal protein, fresh fruit and vegetables, all of which cost more, according to studies.

articles.title: Scottish Labour’s new leader backs Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gasfields
articles.description: Michael Marra supports development of the North Sea sites, calling for a ‘more rational’ approach to energy policy Scottish Labour’s new leader Michael Marra has backed the development of the Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gasfields in the North Sea in one of his first acts after being elected, calling for a “more rational” approach to energy policy. On Saturday, the MSP for North East Scotland won a near two-thirds majority to lead the party in Holyrood, becoming Scottish Labour’s 11th leader. He replaces Anas Sarwar after his shock decision to resign in July to join Andy Burnham’s new government as a trade minister.

articles.title: Consumer sentiment is in the dumps despite a solid economy. Goldman Sachs blames 'lower happiness'
articles.description: Goldman economist Joseph Briggs said broader pessimism in society may be contributing to struggling consumer sentiment even as the economy chugs along.

articles.title: ‘Way too many guns around’: experts say firearm access key factor in spate of US family killings
articles.description: Acts of ‘familicide’ have increased dramatically this year – in the US, the killer is more likely to have easy access to a gun The US is often known globally for its shocking levels of violence, but acts of “family annihilation” or “familicide” rank among the most disturbing of crimes. They occur when an assailant kills four or more of their own family members and often see the killer also kill themselves. These types of crime have increased dramatically this year, according to data from Northeastern University .

articles.title: The AI kill switch, explained: 'It's not too little, but it's probably too late'
articles.description: As runaway AI fears reach a crescendo, policymakers and tech leaders are weighing the effectiveness of a magic AI stop button known as a kill switch.

articles.title: US fashion CEO resigns after physically restraining animal rights activists
articles.description: Steven Kolb of the Council of Fashion Designers of America was filmed during an altercation at New York fashion week The chief executive of the Council of Fashion Designers of America, Steven Kolb, has resigned after he was filmed physically restraining two animal rights activists during an altercation at New York fashion week. “After 20 years leading the CFDA, I have made the difficult decision to step down as CEO and president,” Kolb said in a statement. “I am enormously proud of what we have built together and believe this is the right moment for both me and the organisation to begin a new chapter.”

articles.title: Students scramble for accommodation after provider goes bust in Dundee
articles.description: Case highlights severe financial strain on sector across UK as string of university housing schemes fail Are you having problems with your accommodation provider? Nearly 70 students in Dundee have been left scrambling to find accommodation for this academic year after the latest in a string of university housing schemes went bust amid severe financial strain on the sector. Students in the city have been forced to find alternative housing and rapidly move their possessions as term begins this month after the collapse of the owner of Marketgait Apartments, a city centre block.

articles.title: Unease in ‘newly independent’ Piddington as world media and Danny Tommo descend
articles.description: As villagers take stock following symbolic vote, some fear far-right weaponisation of asylum dispute and influx of ‘masked people like in Dover’ The first significant event in the newly independent principality of Piddington was a decision to select the newt as the national animal, reflecting optimism that the amphibian’s endangered status might help block plans to open a centre for 1,250 asylum seekers on neighbouring land. The choice was announced on Thursday morning, the day after Piddington announced that villagers had voted overwhelmingly to leave the UK. Parish councillors were also thinking about asking local children to design a flag and considering whether the new principality’s national sport should be cricket or football.

articles.title: Jim Ratcliffe: UK is ‘on the slide’ from days when it had world’s ‘greatest empire’
articles.description: Co-owner of Manchester United says Britain is in decline because of high taxes and immigration The co-owner of Manchester United Sir Jim Ratcliffe has described the UK as being a country “on the slide” from the days when it had “the greatest empire in the world”. Ratcliffe, who founded petrochemicals giant Ineos, and has resided in Monaco, which has a relaxed tax regime, since 2020, said Britain is in decline because of high taxes and immigration.

articles.title: Hundreds evacuated after fire breaks out at seaside hotel in Kent
articles.description: About 280 people taken to safety from the Grand Burstin in Folkestone after blaze thought to have started in basement Hundreds of people have been evacuated from a hotel in Folkestone after a large fire broke out overnight. Emergency services were called just after 1am on Saturday to the Grand Burstin hotel in Folkestone, where a fire is believed to have started in the basement, Kent fire and rescue service said.

articles.title: 特朗普據報將赴機場迎接習近平，待遇比肩教宗和赫魯曉夫
articles.description: 美國總統親赴機場迎接外國元首極為罕見。若不計教宗訪美的特例，這將是超過 60 年來美國總統首次以這種方式迎接他國元首。

articles.title: Trump says U.S. to build a 'large Military presence' in Greenland as part of a security deal with it and Denmark
articles.description: Greenland has maintained it is not for sale, and the European Union earlier this year united to rebuke Trump over his push to acquire the island.

articles.title: Record fuel prices across EU prompt calls for bloc-wide windfall tax on firms
articles.description: German minister says companies are ‘exploiting situation’ in Middle East, as sky-high prices become major domestic issue for leaders European governments have discussed imposing a bloc-wide windfall tax on energy companies, as near-record fuel and gas prices pile pressure on leaders desperate to contain mounting public discontent and the challenge of the far right. With elections due next year in eight EU countries including France, Italy, Spain and Poland, leaders are scrambling to head off the potential fallout from what analysts have warned could be one of the continent’s biggest energy shocks in decades.

articles.title: Shark catch-and-kill order issued after swimmer dies off popular Perth beach
articles.description: Man, 63, fatally bitten by shark at Sorrento beach on Friday morning As the hunt for the animal remained under way on Saturday, the WA fisheries minister, Jackie Jarvis, revealed she had greenlit the order.

articles.title: From ovations in Venice to death threats in Israel: the extreme responses to NAZA documentary
articles.description: As Gaza documentary wins cinematic acclaim, its directors face vitriol in Israel amid a febrile election campaign First there was a moment of stunned silence. Then, in the Sala Grande, the main screening hall of the Venice film festival within the Palazzo del Cinema, the audience stood almost as one and turned to applaud the film-makers for 25 minutes. The film the audience had watched for 80 harrowing minutes was the Gaza documentary NAZA, which has been produced by the Guardian.

articles.title: A new arms race is unfolding on the ocean floor
articles.description: Countries and companies are investing in technologies for underwater use amid concerns about the vulnerability of critical infrastructure on the ocean floor.

articles.title: ‘My fear was too great’: the Pussy Riot member recruited by Russian spies to inform on fellow activists
articles.description: Exclusive: In her first media interview since fleeing Russia, Rita Flores describes her three years of being run by the FSB First came the blackmail and death threats to secure cooperation, then came a series of tasks, each more sinister than the last: to inform on fellow activists, to elicit personal information from protest-minded artists and – eventually – to help with a plot to kidnap and murder a Kremlin enemy. That is how Rita Flores, a 29-year-old Russian artist, activist and former member of the Pussy Riot collective , described her recruitment and three-year handling by officers from Russia’s FSB security service, a cooperation she only broke when she fled the country last month.

articles.title: Google's Gemini becomes latest AI model to break out and hack computer systems
articles.description: The disclosure comes as scrutiny over misbehaving artificial intelligence intensifies in Washington and Silicon Valley.

articles.title: US and Denmark reach security deal after Trump’s threats to take over Greenland
articles.description: The agreement would allow the US to expand its military presence, while Denmark and Greenland say it preserves their sovereignty and right to self-determination Donald Trump announced on Friday that the US had struck an Arctic security pact with the leaders of Denmark and Greenland, after threatening for much of his second term to annex the semi-autonomous Danish territory by force. The full scope of the deal Trump described as “very important, historic, and special” was not immediately clear. But soon after his announcement in a post on Truth Social, the leaders of Denmark and Greenland issued statements indicating the deal would be signed by the three governments on the sidelines of the United Nations general assembly in New York City next week.

articles.title: Men deported from US bound and beaten in Equatorial Guinea detention hotel, lawyers say
articles.description: Group trapped at Hotel Bamy after US removal as rights groups sound alarm over poor conditions and violence Two men that the Trump administration expelled to Equatorial Guinea were bound, fitted with bags over their heads, beaten and pushed down a flight of stairs, all in plain view of other US deportees, according to witnesses and human rights lawyers. The men – one from Egypt and one from Eritrea – were then taken to a prison. About 30 detainees from the US remain trapped at a hotel in the outskirts of the coastal city of Malabo after being deported from the US. Detainees have said they believe the men were beaten for telling the press and human rights advocates about the poor conditions and violence inside the hotel, and that they are haunted by flashbacks and terrified they will be retaliated against next.

articles.title: Latvia’s president warns that Europe is not up to date with drone and aerial warfare in Ukraine
articles.description: Edgars Rinkēvičs says drone warfare in Ukraine is moving at ‘lightning speed’ and efforts to prepare for an aerial war could be obsolete by next year Latvia’s president has warned that Europe is not keeping up with developments of drone and aerial warfare in Ukraine and that most countries in Nato could not repulse an attack by Russian missiles if the conflict expands. The remarks came during a Guardian interview in Washington DC in which Edgars Rinkēvičs said that the technological developments in drone warfare in Ukraine are moving at “lightning speed” and that current efforts to prepare for an aerial war could be obsolete by the middle of next year.

articles.title: Anthropic selects Accenture as first embedded evaluator to help implement Amodei's slowdown proposal
articles.description: Anthropic and OpenAI have been under intense scrutiny after researchers warned about the potential for AI to cause catastrophic harm to humanity.

articles.title: OpenAI's latest AI revelation is a 'serious situation,' Microsoft's Suleyman tells CNBC
articles.description: Suleyman joined "Squawk Box" to discuss OpenAI's latest incidents of "concerning model behavior" disclosed earlier this week.

articles.title: AI cloud provider Nscale files to go public
articles.description: Nscale is the latest artificial intelligence neocloud to turn to public markets.

articles.title: Nike parts ways with Kylian Mbappé; soccer superstar signs with On
articles.description: Mbappe had been signed with Nike for roughly two decades, and his agreement with On is the first it has made with a soccer player.

articles.title: Elon Musk talks up AI safety while fighting regulation in wild week of strange alliances
articles.description: In the past week, Musk has agreed with the CEOs of Anthropic and OpenAI, while getting contradicted by President Trump and Nvidia's Jensen Huang.

articles.title: California Gov. Newsom issues executive order to rein in AI 'before it's too late'
articles.description: California Gov. Gavin Newsom and other 2028 Democratic presidential hopefuls have called for a more aggressive approach to addressing AI fears.

articles.title: Fed staff should have known Silicon Valley Bank was vulnerable, new report finds
articles.description: Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said a new report indicates the central bank's staff missed signs ahead of Silicon Valley Bank's 2023 failure.

articles.title: Three words from Kevin Warsh have Wall Street wondering how far the Fed will go with rate hikes
articles.description: The chairman both explained this week's decision to raise interest rates, and raised vexing questions about what comes next

articles.title: Ticket prices rise for Macklemore solo concert after Ed Sheeran tour removal
articles.description: Ticket prices are rising for Macklemore's upcoming solo concert after the rapper was removed from Ed Sheeran's tour for making pro-Palestine comments.

articles.title: JPMorgan, Citigroup CEOs attending Trump's state dinner for China's Xi: Sources
articles.description: Dimon and Fraser join OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Nvidia chief Jensen Huang and others who are reportedly planning to attend the Trump-Xi state dinner.

articles.title: Survivors recount panic and struggle to breathe in Nigerian prison cell where 37 died
articles.description: Police fire teargas as protests break out in city of Minna after deaths of suspected illegal goldminers, many of whom were children Survivors from a prison cell in Nigeria where 37 suspected illegal goldminers died while in the custody of a paramilitary group this week have recounted their panic and struggle for breath, as police on Friday fired teargas at people protesting against the deaths and imposed an overnight curfew in the city of Minna. The victims – many of whom were children – were found dead on Thursday in the cells of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), which had raided suspected illegal goldmines and ⁠locked up dozens of miners in the city, the state capital of the mineral-rich state of Niger.

articles.title: Auto industry urges Trump to bar Chinese automakers in U.S. ahead of Xi visit
articles.description: Leaders of six major auto trade groups joined to sign a letter to the president.

articles.title: Brazil’s Lula announces higher welfare payments and free weight-loss jabs ahead of election
articles.description: Critics say moves from leftwing incumbent president are electorally motivated two weeks before Brazil’s elections Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has announced a 15% increase in the country’s main cash-transfer programme for poor families, as well as free weight-loss jabs, prompting criticism from opponents who say the moves are electorally motivated just two weeks before the presidential election. On 4 October, the leftwing incumbent will face the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, who has been gaining ground in recent weeks.

articles.title: AirAsia's Fernandes refutes financial concerns, points to new growth plans
articles.description: AirAsia's Tony Fernandes pushed back against a report raising concerns over the airline’s financial health, while signaling plans to resume growth.

articles.title: Disney names CTO for the first time as media giant expands tech push
articles.description: Disney has hired a chief technology officer, a newly minted role for the company, as it looks to further its embrace of tech under CEO Josh D'Amaro.

articles.title: StubHub shares tick higher for third day in a row after Citi upgrade
articles.description: Analyst Jason Bazinet raised his rating to buy from neutral.

articles.title: Alleged underworld supporters and unfounded health claims: One Nation rolls out more Victorian election candidates
articles.description: Party has unveiled a steady stream of contenders for state election, including a former councillor who lost his licence for drink-driving Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast Candidates contesting the Victorian state election for One Nation include a former Liberal who has won support from alleged underworld figures, a naturopath who has endorsed Donald Trump’s unfounded claim that paracetamol is linked to autism and a former shire councillor who lost his licence for drink-driving. Pauline Hanson announced who would be her party’s upper house candidates and Victorian leader, Warren Pickering, at a press conference last month . Since then One Nation has used social media to unveil a steady stream of candidates, with 51 of the 88 lower house spots now filled.

articles.title: Swedish teenager jailed for attempted murder, rape and assault committed online, with victims in Germany and Australia
articles.description: Eighteen-year-old known as Chai was active in networks notorious for their sadistic exploitation of young people A Swedish teenager known as Chai has been sentenced to more than 10 years in jail for attempted murder, rape and aggravated assault – crimes committed via the internet, including against a teenage girl in Australia . The district court found that Chai, 18, was active in online networks notorious for their sadistic extortion of young and vulnerable people, coercing them to create sexually explicit material or engage in acts of violence – and for the youth of those involved. In Australia, support is available at Beyond Blue on 1300 22 4636, Lifeline on 13 11 14, and at MensLine on 1300 789 978. In the UK, the charity Mind is available on 0300 123 3393 and Childline on 0800 1111. In the US, call or text Mental Health America at 988 or chat 988lifeline.org.

articles.title: Yemen’s anti-Houthi forces launch inquest into sudden military collapse
articles.description: Rout raises questions about coordination and morale as some politicians claim billions of dollars were offered to persuade forces to abandon position A bitter inquest is under way among Yemen’s anti-Houthi forces as to how what was being billed as a decisive assault on Sana’a, the Houthi-controlled capital, suddenly collapsed into a military rout. More than 15 brigades were defeated as the country’s entire west coast fell into Houthi hands. Efforts are now being made to reorganise the anti-Houthi forces representing the UN-recognised Yemeni government in order to capture the Kahbob mountains, a strategic point from which to restrict Houthi forces moving closer to the crucial Bab al-Mandab strait.

articles.title: British Sikh man granted bail in India nine years after arrest
articles.description: Jagtar Singh Johal, from Scotland, was arrested after wedding in Punjab on alleged terrorism offences Jagtar Singh Johal, a British Sikh man who was arrested in India in 2017 in connection with alleged terrorism offences, has been granted bail by a Delhi court. Johal, from Scotland, was arrested for his alleged role in funding the Khalistan Liberation Force, which had carried out targeted killings in India’s Punjab region.

articles.title: Putin targets Nestle's Russian business as Kremlin tightens grip on Western assets
articles.description: Nestlé is assessing its options after Russia placed the Swiss food giant’s local assets under temporary external administration.

articles.title: Warren Buffett steps down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway: 'Father Time always wins'
articles.description: Buffett's son Howard will replace him as chairman, as dictated by a long-standing succession plan, Berkshire said.

articles.title: British woman who was kidnapped in Malawi rescued by police after shootout
articles.description: Four of Nurat Osman’s alleged abductors were killed during rescue after she was taken from outside her home last week A British woman kidnapped in Malawi last week has been rescued by police after a shootout in which four of her alleged abductors were killed. Nusrat Osman was abducted outside her home in the southern city of Blantyre on 11 September at about 12.30pm. Police had offered a reward of 30m Malawi kwacha (£12,950) for information leading to her rescue and the arrest of the perpetrators.

articles.title: 對台軍售成「特習會」談判籌碼？北京警告或取消峰會施壓特朗普
articles.description: 中美兩國元首本月稍後預定在華府舉行的「特習會」，是全球矚目的外交焦點，中方仍未公布行程。據報北京警告若華府會前批准新一輪百億美元對台軍售，或將取消峰會。

articles.title: Australian man accused of murdering Thai teenager and putting body in suitcase pleads not guilty
articles.description: Simon Peter Carman appeared in a Pattaya court on Friday charged with killing Tunchanok Donhomla An Australian man accused of murdering a Thai teenager and putting her body in a suitcase pleaded not guilty on Friday in a hearing in the seaside resort city of Pattaya, a court official said. Simon Peter Carman, 45, was arrested in June after 17-year-old Tunchanok Donhomla was reported missing in Pattaya City, about 150km south-east of Bangkok. A suitcase containing her body was found shortly after.

articles.title: Louisiana firefighters find feline native to sub-Saharan Africa while responding to house fire
articles.description: The African serval, illegally enclosed in the back yard, was subdued and transferred to an animal welfare facility Louisiana firefighters responding to a small house blaze found a wildcat native to sub-Saharan Africa illegally enclosed in the back yard, prompting an animal welfare agency to seek placing the creature in an appropriate environment, according to officials. Firefighters investigating a report of a minor fire at a home in the suburban New Orleans community of Marrero on Tuesday spotted the cat in question – an African serval – behind the residence in a chain-linked enclosure resembling a cramped baseball batting cage, a spokesperson for the local animal protection services said.

articles.title: Iranian actor Laleh Marzban faces severe threats after Venice film festival speech
articles.description: Marzban, who won a best actress award for her portrayal of a woman held hostage by her father in Falling House, has received condemnations from authorities after dedicating her prize to ‘the women of Iran’ An Iranian actress who won the best newcomer award at the Venice film festival has come under severe attack from the country’s authorities and state media after highlighting the plight of women in Iran in her acceptance speech. Laleh Marzban last Saturday won the best actress award in the Orizzonti sidebar competition for emerging talent, for her role in Mohsen Gharaei’s Falling House , a film revolving around three generations of women who are incarcerated in their own home by the family’s father.

articles.title: 人類真的可能被AI滅絕？我們可以如何阻止？
articles.description: 人工智能（AI）快速發展之際，AI界對其潛在風險的公開討論也越來越多。部分科學家甚至估計，未來十年AI導致人類滅絕的可能性超過一成。

articles.title: Anthropic and OpenAI hunt for smaller data center deals, sources tell CNBC, in race to deploy AI capacity
articles.description: Anthropic and OpenAI have announced a flurry of AI infrastructure deals over the past year as demand booms.

articles.title: An intense boardroom battle is brewing at India's giant Tata Group
articles.description: In 10 years, India's leading multinational conglomerate, the Tata Group, is facing a new power struggle between the chairman of Tata Sons and Tata Trusts.

articles.title: 「運動員無法伸直雙腿睡覺」：日本亞運為何爆發住宿爭議？
articles.description: 亞運選手將入住木製貨櫃屋或一艘意大利郵輪。韓國代表團批評，貨櫃屋宿舍水管漏水，且床舖太小，運動員甚至無法伸直雙腿睡覺。

articles.title: Andrew Hastie says AI advised him to reply ‘congratulations!’ to man who planned to end life with assisted dying
articles.description: Liberal MP speaks of AI’s shortcomings as cyber chief tells inquiry the tech is needed to fend off ‘highly capable malicious cyber actors’ Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast When a man with a terminal illness wrote to his local MP Andrew Hastie, telling him he planned on ending his own life with voluntary assisted dying, Microsoft Copilot suggested Hastie reply with “congratulations!”, “great to hear from you” or “that is wonderful news!”. Hastie shared the episode at a parliamentary inquiry on Friday to underline the shortcomings of the American-run software as he called for AI run by Australians.

articles.title: Hyrox失禁風波：澳洲選手道歉、主辦方承諾退款
articles.description: Hyrox已更新賽例，明文規定若參賽者的「血液、嘔吐物、尿液或糞便」構成健康風險，可被要求退賽。

articles.title: Weather tracker: Thunderstorms hit Spain as Japan braces for typhoon
articles.description: At least one person dead as stormy weather causes severe flooding in Barcelona and Valencia Intense and slow-moving thunderstorms broke out on Wednesday afternoon across parts of eastern Spain, bringing some severe flooding and killing at least one person . Storms first struck over the Castilla-La Mancha region during the afternoon before passing over Spain’s east coast, becoming very slow-moving and continuing overnight. Torrential rainfall, strong winds and large hail were reported in Valencia and Barcelona, causing widespread flooding in both cities. Weather stations west of Barcelona recorded some of the highest totals with more than 100mm (4in) of rain falling in the space of a few hours, and locally 70mm in just 30 minutes in the early hours of Thursday morning. Cars and roads were submerged, and flights were cancelled across the region.

articles.title: ‘We have something that will kill Elliott’: Icac questions former Labor councillor over message
articles.description: Sharangan Maheswaran denies message he received about NSW minister was related to work for fugitive property developer Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast A former Labor councillor says he had a “common interest” with a conservative Liberal operative, but denied that a message he received about damaging the reputation of NSW Liberal minister David Elliott was related to political work for a fugitive property developer, an inquiry has heard. Sharangan Maheswaran told the Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) on Friday that a message sent to him by lobbyist Jeremy Greenwood claiming “We have something that will kill Elliott” did not relate to work by Greenwood’s company Beckington for Jean Nassif.

articles.title: ‘We demand the truth’: Olga Tokarczuk and JM Coetzee lead calls for proof of life of disappeared Eritrean writers
articles.description: More than 180 writers sign letter renewing calls for information on 12 authors detained incommunicado since 2001 crackdown on free speech by Isaias Afwerki More than 180 writers have signed a letter to Eritrean president Isaias Afwerki calling for proof of life for 12 writers arrested in 2001. Nobel laureates Olga Tokarczuk and JM Coetzee join prominent writers including Colm Tóibín, Elif Shafak, Isabel Allende, Ben Okri, Yann Martel, Kamila Shamsie and Tsitsi Dangarembga in signing the letter organised by PEN International and dated 18 September, marking 25 years since a government crackdown on the independent press. “Within days, Eritrea’s free press and the nation’s independent voices were systematically crushed,” opens the letter.

articles.title: Trump administration advances $24.3 billion fighter jet deal to Saudi Arabia as Houthis escalate attacks
articles.description: The deal comes as Iran-backed Houthis escalate attacks on Saudi Arabia and seek control of the strategically important Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

articles.title: Putin braces for election stress test as Russians ‘feel the pain’ of struggling economy
articles.description: Russia’s upcoming election is expected to cement United Russia’s dominance, but voter turnout and its margin of victory could offer clues to public discontent.

articles.title: Why Japan’s markets flipped the usual script after central bank rate hike
articles.description: The yen weakened past 157 against the dollar, the yield on the 10-year Japanese Government Bond slipped, while the Nikkei 225 gained 1.5%.

articles.title: Japan raises interest rates to 31-year high to curb impact of rising prices
articles.description: Increase from 1% to 1.25% follows US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank tightening monetary policy Business live – latest updates Japan’s central bank has increased interest rates to a fresh 31-year high as it attempts to combat global inflation linked to the war in Iran. The Bank of Japan (BoJ) voted to raise its target interest rate from 1% to 1.25%, the highest level since 1995.

articles.title: South Korea will not send military to support US war on Iran, defying Trump pressure
articles.description: Seoul resolves recent speculation over sending military to strait of Hormuz, saying ‘there won’t be deployment that would involve or enter war’ South Korea’s president, Lee Jae Myung, has said he will ⁠not deploy the military to the ⁠Middle East in a way ​that could draw the country into conflict, resisting calls from Donald Trump to support his war in Iran. “There won’t be deployment that would involve or enter war. I can tell you that very clearly,” Lee said at a ⁠news conference on Friday. “We won’t deploy military assets in any form to that end.”

articles.title: 美籍緬甸裔學者涉間諜罪在華監禁　其妻籲特朗普晤習近平時重提此案

articles.title: New cat species identified for first time in more than a century in Bolivia
articles.description: New species of wild feline was discovered in Bolivia’s Yungas forest that is smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat A diminutive wild cat that inhabits Bolivia’s ⁠cloud forest has been identified as a previously unknown species, marking the first time a new living feline species has been formally named and described in more than a century. The cat, called tilcayo by local communities, is part of a group called tiger ⁠cats found across much of South ⁠America. It was found in Bolivia’s ​lush Yungas forest, a mountainous region where forests are often covered by clouds and surrounded by high humidity, according to researchers. It measures about 18in (46cm) long and weighs about 3lb (1.4kg), making it smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat.

articles.title: All smiles in Strasbourg but uncertainty clouds Canada’s EU membership plan

Politicians queued to shake his hand and take selfies. One described the speech as a historic moment. “Europe has extended a hand, and Canada has taken it,” said the German Green MEP Terry Reintke, who borrowed a Canadian ice hockey shirt for the occasion.

articles.title: IS member sentenced to 20 years in prison for role in 2021 Kabul airport bombing
articles.description: Mohammad Sharifullah, 28, was convicted of aiding the terrorist group that took credit for the suicide bombing An Islamic State group member was sentenced on Wednesday to 20 years in prison for aiding the terrorist organization that took credit for a suicide bombing that killed 13 US service members and about 160 Afghans at the Kabul airport five years ago during the US military’s chaotic withdrawal from the country. A federal jury in Virginia had convicted Mohammad Sharifullah in April of providing material support to the IS affiliate known as Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP). But jurors could not agree whether he bore some responsibility for the airport bombing on 26 August 2021.

articles.title: Climate crisis probably weakened glacier that caused devastating Nepal-Tibet floods, first study finds
articles.description: Scientists say global heating was a destabilising factor in collapse of 200,000 sq metre glacier in August Climate breakdown probably weakened the glacier that collapsed causing catastrophic floods and killing over a thousand people in Nepal and Tibet last month, the first scientific study of the disaster has found. Researchers identified unusually warm conditions before the glacier’s collapse , which sent an avalanche of 110m cubic metres (3.885bn cu ft) of snow and ice into the valley below. This triggered flash floods on an almost unprecedented scale, hitting communities downstream without warning.

articles.title: Battle of Chile director Patricio Guzmán dies aged 85
articles.description: Passionate documentary maker won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The Battle of Chile and Nostalgia for the Light, has died aged 85. According to Chilean news outlet Emol , Guzmán died on Tuesday in Paris after a cardiorespiratory arrest. Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. He later told the Guardian : “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”

articles.title: People protecting nature and land set up self-defence units amid threat of murder
articles.description: Defenders of forests and rivers killed at rate of one every three days in 2025, with 85% of deaths in Latin America Nature and land defenders were murdered at the rate of one every three days last year, prompting many communities to set up self-defence units, according to the latest annual death toll by the independent watchdog Global Witness. Organised crime groups or professional killers were implicated in more than a third of the 124 killings of defenders in 2025 as narco-trafficking activities overlapped with intrusions into indigenous territories and environmental crime, such as illegal logging and wildcat gold mining.

articles.title: What would it take to make India’s cities better – and safer?

Plus, Ahmedabad’s ace newspaper delivery driver goes viral • Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here Recently, I may have saved a woman’s life on the road. Somehow, this was something I had expected to happen. On that day, I saw a truck leave a construction site with a tangled wire trailing behind. I frantically looked to see what the wire was attached to and spotted the scaffolding a few meters ahead. I shrieked and grabbed the hand of the woman walking in front of me just as the metal pipes came crashing down. We hugged for a brief second, and then walked our separate ways.
